subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should deferred context-engine maintenance permanently use this new opt-in timeout plus host-side fence contract, or should it inherit a different host-owned timeout and cancellation policy?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but automation cannot choose a permanent config surface or define how far OpenClaw promises to cancel third-party context-engine work after releasing the session lane.

options.title: Approve the opt-in contract
options.body: Keep the new disabled-by-default setting and host-owned fence because it resolves the observed stall without changing existing deployments, while documenting that plugin-owned work may continue.

options.title: Reuse a host safety budget
options.body: Replace the new setting with an existing canonical timeout policy, accepting that maintainers must define safe upgrade behavior for legitimately long maintenance runs.

options.title: Defer cancellation design
options.body: Split out the stalled-warning backoff and pause the timeout work until the context-engine lifecycle exposes a maintainer-approved cancellation contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Keep the new disabled-by-default setting and host-owned fence because it resolves the observed stall without changing existing deployments, while documenting that plugin-owned work may continue.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history ties jalehman to introduction of the context-engine runtime and compaction boundary whose permanent contract is being changed.
